verdict.rationale: Antigravity documents Hooks, which run custom scripts or shell commands at specific points in the agent's execution loop. That is a real event-to-action trigger, but it is scoped to agent-loop events only. Rules (Manual/Always On/Model Decision/Glob activation) are constraints the agent follows, not triggered actions. Scheduled Tasks are cron-based recurring runs, not event triggers, so neither counts toward this story. Missing for 10: a documented list of hook events, triggers on external events (file changes, git, CI, webhooks), conditional rule-to-action configuration detail, and hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: Hooks allow you to run custom scripts or shell commands at specific points during Antigravity’s execution loop.
